items_missed: Called the customer 'Joe' for the entire first half of the call — her name is Jill; never confirmed the name and only got it right in the sign-off
No agenda statement — asked 'do you have a few minutes to go over the estimate?' but never framed the structure or the 10-15 minute length, and never asked 'sound good?'
No 'anything you're particularly worried about with this move?' stressor question
Never asked about access concerns — parking, truck access, HOA restrictions at either address (new-build neighborhood at Glenn Heights is a real risk)
Never asked about long walks, narrow hallways or tight turns — only asked about specialty items
Never asked how many boxes the customer already has packed, despite her volunteering that the whole garage is already in totes — that directly changes the pack-day estimate
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned — said only 'insurance' as a line item in the hourly rate
No 'no hidden fees' pitch (no credit card fees / no fuel surcharge / no assembly fees) — only mentioned no card fee, and that came after the customer asked about payment
Section 4 Clock almost entirely skipped — no 'clock starts on site when the contract opens', no 2.5-hour minimum, no 15-minute prorated increments
Save Your Ass prep speech never delivered — no 'prep before move day = shorter move = lower bill', no carload tip
Never explained the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email or asked her to reply with corrections
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' — only offered email/phone as channels
Never gave office hours or a direct way to reach him
top_strength: Outstanding budget-conscious framing — when Jill floated a $6,500 number, Chris ran a real worked example (four-man team, six hours each day, ~$300 in materials, $150 trip fee) landing near $5,000, and honestly told her he did not think it would hit fourteen hours instead of letting her over-budget. He also handled the 500 lb solid-wood island proactively with dollies and the lift gate, which visibly relieved a concern she had raised herself.
coaching_note: Get the customer's name right and use it. Chris opened with 'Hey Joe, how are you?' and stayed on the wrong name for most of a 17-minute call to a woman named Jill, only correcting at the goodbye. Confirming the name at the top ('I have Jill Ganther on the quote form — is that right?') costs five seconds and is the cheapest trust-builder on the call. Second priority: he sold this move on price and process alone and left every Einstein differentiator on the table — No Worries $2,000 coverage, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee were all unsaid on a call where the customer volunteered she was comparing quotes and Einstein was already cheaper. Those three are what keep the deal when the competitor drops their number in the next two weeks.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and affirming ('absolutely', 'I totally get it', 'for sure'), landed a genuine laugh with the 'nothing wrong with having TVs in every room' line, and the customer ended openly enthusiastic — held back from a 5 only by the wrong-name issue and near-zero name use.
audio_review_reason: Transcript is heavily garbled through the pricing explanation ('Foran team', 'Beever long take', 'ward road boxes', 'dal spread'), so clarity and pace cannot be judged reliably from text — worth confirming by audio whether Chris is rushing or mumbling through the rate breakdown, which is the highest-stakes part of this call.
